conventions.statement: If l₀ is not an element of the lattice of L, no term is suppressed and the result equals the full ℘' series over all lattice points.
conventions.note: The condition l.1 = l₀ is never satisfied, so every summand is included unchanged.

conventions.point: z equals a lattice point other than l₀
conventions.statement: When z is a lattice point distinct from l₀, the sum contains a term of the form −2/(z − z)³, which is not analytically meaningful; Lean's tsum returns a junk value because the family is not summable.
conventions.note: This is the standard pole location of ℘'; removing l₀ does not remove other poles.

conventions.point: z equals l₀ (and l₀ is in the lattice)
conventions.statement: When z = l₀ ∈ Λ, the diverging term −2/(z − l₀)³ has been zeroed out, and the remaining sum is finite and well-defined.
conventions.note: This is the primary use case: studying the behavior of ℘' near l₀ without the pole contribution from l₀ itself.

facts.statement: ∀ (L : PeriodPair) (l₀ z : ℂ), VTask.derivWeierstrassPExcept L l₀ z = -VTask.derivWeierstrassPExcept L l₀ z → VTask.derivWeierstrassPExcept L l₀ z = 0

facts.statement: ∀ (L : PeriodPair) (l₀ : ℂ), ∃ z₁ z₂ : ℂ, VTask.derivWeierstrassPExcept L l₀ z₁ = VTask.derivWeierstrassPExcept L l₀ z₁ ∧ VTask.derivWeierstrassPExcept L l₀ z₂ = VTask.derivWeierstrassPExcept L l₀ z₂
